newsitem.title: USA: Oak Technology files patent complaint.
newsitem.headline: Oak Technology files patent complaint.

text.p: Oak Technology Inc Tuesday said it filed a complaint with the U.S. International Trade Commission against nine companies alleging a violation of trade laws for importing or selling products that Oak believes infringe on two of its patents.

Oak makes CD-ROM controllers that are used in computers. One patent in question describes a process that reduces the storage space and time needed for a computer to locate information on a CD-ROM. A second describes how CD-ROM drives communicate with other devices in the computer.
Oak has asked the commission to investigate the companies and issue an order barring imports into the United States of the products that allegedly infringe on the patents.
The nine companies are Winbond Electronics Corp of Taiwan and its U.S. affiliate Winbond Electronics North American Corp; Wearnes Technology Ltd of Singapore and Wearnes Electronics Malaysia S.B.

Also based in Tawain are United Microelectronics Corp, Lite-On Group, Lite-On Technology Corp and Behavior Tech Computer Corp. Finally Behavior's U.S. unit, Behavior Tech Computer (USA) Corp, is named as well.
Oak shares ended trading up 17/32 at 10-25/32
